answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with time-locked identity maturation: every new identity starts at zero influence, like a zephyr that has not yet gathered force, and earns weight only through a long, glacier-slow history of verifiable useful work. Influence accrues on a fixed schedule no payment can accelerate, so a flood of fresh identities stays weightless however many are spawned. Idle reputation decays, and detected misbehavior burns the accumulated history, pushing the offender back to the horizon of zero trust.
